status: root source-stage policy; final corpus validation pending
source_version: Language in India 13(7), July 2013; Aranadan chapter pp.9–11
scope: Complete source-defined Aranadan chapter plus source-wide check for attributed additional occurrences; not a claim that all chapters of the multilingual book are ingested
licence: No explicit open reuse licence established. Publisher provides free access; do not describe that as CC licensing. Import attributed lexical facts and source-specific analyses; retain full original PDF outside canonical source assets.
attribution: Nair is the primary chapter author. The preface describes compiled material extended by incomplete fieldwork, without assigning all Aranadan examples to field elicitation. Usha1992 is reported bibliography, not an independently collated lexical source.
extraction: Native positioned PDF text reconciled with original images; no OCR engine used for this chapter

transcription.reason: The source supplies Roman notation with doubled vowels, nasal tildes, lower dots and drawn low lines, but no complete phonemic conversion key. Preserve these distinctions instead of silently assigning IPA values or collapsing visually distinct lower marks. Native-font repairs recover visible characters only; they are not a phonemic conversion.
transcription.Original: Reviewed source transcription with exact case and doubled vowels; NFC combining-dot/tilde equivalents; explicit low lines retained separately
transcription.Form: Literal-preservation route, matching reviewed Original apart from documented generic display punctuation handling
validation_required: All emitted forms contain no private-use characters or replacement glyphs
Every native-font or drawn-mark repair has original-position evidence
Actual parser preserves all rows, fields, boundaries and source keys
NFC/NFD inputs preserve the same visible distinctions
No automatic comma/slash expansion or guessed phonological substitution

identity: Existing Aranadan, Malayalam and Kannada bases; distribution places do not identify separate elicited dialects or coordinates
